facts.text: Specimens were annealed under argon at 1100 °C for 1 h or at 1200 and 1300 °C for 30 min, then water-quenched to room temperature.
Rockwell C hardness was measured with a 1471 N load, a 5 s dwell, and five indentations for each annealing condition.
Phase separation and ordering were evaluated using XRD, SEM, SADP/dark-field TEM, and STEM–EDS.
During cooling, the high-temperature disordered BCC phase was inferred to undergo spinodal decomposition into Ni–Al-lean BCC1 and Ni–Al-rich BCC2 regions.
Below the ordering transition, the Ni–Al-rich BCC products ordered into the B2 structure.
The quenched microstructure was reciprocal and hierarchical: a BCC matrix contained B2 particles, while the larger B2 particles contained BCC nanoparticles.
Phase boundaries, compositional modulation, and ordered B2 domains were proposed to impede dislocation motion and thereby increase hardness.
Increasing the annealing temperature from 1100 to 1300 °C before quenching increased the BCC fraction and the reported density of ordered B2 precipitates.
Hardness increased monotonically with annealing temperature relative to the 1100 °C annealed-and-quenched baseline.
The measured hardness values were 38.96 ± 0.38 HRC at 1100 °C, 42.82 ± 0.31 HRC at 1200 °C, and 50.42 ± 0.56 HRC at 1300 °C.
After the 1300 °C treatment, the BCC matrix contained approximately 50 vol.% fine B2 particles, with larger B2 particles about 50–100 nm and matrix B2 nanoparticles about 2–10 nm in size.

For the 1300 °C condition, the matrix was approximately Cr49Co19Fe20Ni11Al1, whereas the fine particles were approximately Cr14Co13Fe12Ni38Al23, confirming Ni–Al enrichment of B2 and Co–Cr–Fe enrichment of BCC.
